subdomain: 3.7 Evaluate connection protocols and select the appropriate integration mechanism (MCP, API/CLI, agent-to-agent)

en.question: A reusable tool service must support both a client-launched local worker and an independently hosted remote endpoint. All participating clients and servers target MCP 2026-07-28; compatibility with older initialization-based revisions is out of scope. Which transport and request-metadata decisions match that exact version? Select 2 answers.

options.text: Establish protocol version and capabilities only through a mandatory connection-scoped initialize handshake.
options.note: The current version carries this metadata per request. The transport overview discusses connection-scoped initialization as an earlier-revision compatibility model, not the required current contract.

options.text: Use stdio for the client-launched worker and Streamable HTTP with per-message POSTs and JSON or request-scoped SSE replies for the remote endpoint.
options.note: These are the documented standard bindings for the two deployment shapes. The framing and delivery differ while the core MCP protocol semantics remain the same.

options.text: Require a persistent standalone SSE connection before any remote tool request because all MCP HTTP communication depends on that session.
options.note: MCP 2026-07-28 describes per-message HTTP POSTs with JSON-object or request-scoped SSE responses. A mandatory persistent SSE session is not that binding's transport contract.

options.text: Carry protocol version and client capabilities in the request body's _meta fields, treating the body as authoritative if the binding mirrors metadata.
options.note: This version puts protocol metadata in each request body. Selected values may also be mirrored by the HTTP binding, but the body remains the source of truth.
